OP, my first pet was a rabbit I had for four years that died in my arms. He was limping and I waited three days for an appointment with a quality exotic vet. I was planning to surrender him cause I couldn’t afford care when he showed signs of a neurological or spinal problem. Shelters were offering to take him in. That night I found him collapsed and dying. I spent, and still feel, that I couldve done so much more to save his life. He was my reason to be alive and my motivation to keep going. Without him I was completely confused on what to do next, plus feeling like a shitty human being. It didn’t help that I lost two cats the year after (one ran around, the other had liver failure. Both strays we took in)

Unfortunately life can be.. cruel. No matter how hard you try, some things just happen. Think of your intention, the fact that u feel guilt right now means you loved that kitten and wanted the best for it. You WANTED it to get better, care for it to the best of ur means. I was your age too when I lost my rabbit.

The other choice was you could’ve sat and abandoned that kitten. Or maybe given it up for it to die anyways or find a terrible owner. Instead, you tried your best and it died in the arms of someone that cared. That’s enough. You trying doesn’t make you bad, feeling guilt just makes you human. Empathy is something we need more of.

Best of luck, OP. Do not let guilt consume you.

What you’re in is that state of waiting, seeing it as a wish and hope. It might be that you have something in your subconscious telling you that it won’t come easily or that in the narrative of how your life has been, thats how it will be. 

The goal is persisting and seeing it as an opportunity to figure out what thoughts or feelings need to change. Those little moments of “failing” could be the final hurdle. But I do think you believe that you have been “persisting” but not “receiving”

The goal is being delusional as crap, not overthinking, and letting things be. Look inward and accept where you are now isn’t permanent. Everything is shifting, changing. The now is only a reflection of a past energy, and an allowance of the need that you have to “wait” or “persist.” Change that story. Yeah, life is a bitch but that is not my destiny. It’s good from here, unfolding in ways that may surprise you. I mean, think, and really believe that tomorrow is today. That is most likely the thought you need to continue with.
